assign.brief: spacing-apply — apply the spacing study's one bug fix, build the ceilings comparison, fix the cms constant

log.msg: root cause traced live (Playwright getComputedStyle, not inferred): .page-previews margin-block-start used the AMBIENT inherited --flow, which .page-column-prose scopes to 0.8em for every /imagine/ column — but its .md.flow prose neighbours re-trigger framework.css's :where(.flow){--flow:2em} on themselves, so they escape that scoping and the wall doesn't. Confirmed on blogx@1280: wall margin-top computed 10.8288px (=0.8em), neighbour computed 27.072px (=2em) — exactly the study's 2.5x.

fix: Page.css:637 .page-previews rule — --gap: 0.8em -> var(--gap-default), plus a new margin-block: var(--gap-default) (higher specificity than the (0,0,0) :where(.flow) rule in the same theme layer, so it wins outright). Chose --gap-default over var(--flow) because --flow IS the buggy, scoped value already in play; --gap-default is the site's own responsive clamp, independent of the flow-scoping trap, and already this rule's own gap fallback.

re-measured the 3 confirmed pairs (blogx/platform/stream): before 2.50x at both 1280 and 3440 (constant, since both old values were flat em multiples of the same font-size); after 2.00x @1280, 1.37x @3440 -- all three, both widths, under 2.5x.

45-comparison re-shoot: walked all 22 realm landing pages at 1280+3440 (script in scratchpad/spacing-apply/reshoot.mjs), found 12 realms with a live .page-previews wall (13th is /imagine/'s own Start rail, not in the realm list). No x:0 boxes, no new overflow, active-column scrollHeight===clientHeight everywhere -- max added height per page ~13px, no fold regression found.

ceilings page built at public/imagine/design/spacing/ceilings/page.js (not wired into spacing/page.js's children per fence -- mastermind wires it). Finding: raising just the clamp's literal MAX is a no-op at 3440 here (the clamp's preferred branch 0.4em+0.5vw already sits under the current 1.6em cap, confirmed live before shooting) -- so the 3 candidates scale the WHOLE clamp (floor+preferred+ceiling) x1/1.5/2 via a Playwright-injected <style>, never framework.css. 9 crops (<58KB jpg each) shot on cms/paging/stream@3440. Median gap beside the wall: 23.67px / 35.52px / 47.36px. No fold regressions on any candidate (visibleKids unchanged).

cms constant: exhaustive grep of every file under public/imagine/cms/ found ZERO hardcoded em/px vertical-spacing value -- the flatness (1.03x, worst in the study) is Page.css's shared, framework-wide .page-preview{gap:0.6em}/.page-preview-link{gap:0.45em} card-internal constants dominating a tiny sample (cms has only 5 cards and, uniquely among the realm set, NOTHING after its previews wall -- platform, which uses the identical width:"large" word, has real prose after its wall and grows 1.71x, the study's best). Fixed the one real thing in cms/page.js's own gift: added a two-paragraph closing after previews() (platform/blogx/stream all have one). Found in passing: a single-block md() call is adopted as a bare

with NO .flow class, so it inherits the same scoped --flow bug this task just fixed on the wall -- written as a two-paragraph closing specifically to dodge it, with the trap left as a comment.

assign.outcome: **The previews-wall bug fixed at the cause, the ceilings proposal shot, the cms constant found and fixed.** `.page-previews` in `core/Page/Page.css` traded its flat `--gap: 0.8em` for `var(--gap-default)` on both the wall's own grid gap and (new) its entrance/exit margin — the three confirmed pairs drop from a flat 2.50x to 2.00x@1280 / 1.37x@3440, and a 45-comparison re-shoot across all 22 realm landing pages found no new fold or overflow regressions. `/imagine/design/spacing/ceilings/` (new, mastermind wires it as a child) shoots cms/paging/stream@3440 under three token-scaled ceilings via a Playwright-injected `<style>` — never `framework.css` — with medians 23.67 / 35.52 / 47.36px beside the wall. `public/imagine/cms/` carried no hardcoded spacing constant (exhaustive grep confirmed it); its 1.03x was a tiny, card-dominated sample with nothing after the wall (unlike platform, same width word, 1.71x, the study's best) — fixed by adding real closing prose, which also caught a second live instance of this task's own bug (a single-block `md()` inherits the same scoped `--flow` the wall did) and dodged it.
